posts.name: Sayan Ghosh

That means your code is not efficient and is taking longer than allowed.

Try to come up with a more efficient solution.

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
In course portal, if a code takes too long, it is killed to prevent infinite loops.

There is no way to know if a program will halt or not, this is called The Halting Problem by Alan Turing. Therefore, the only way to prevent an infinite loop from a student code to keep on running is to put a time limit on the code and automatically kill it if it is still running. This however will also kill inefficient codes running on large input data (like this question).
